points.en: Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is developed by UNDP and OPHI.
points.hi: Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is developed by UNDP and OPHI.

points.en: It measures poverty beyond income, focusing on deprivations in health, education, and standard of living.
points.hi: It measures poverty beyond income, focusing on deprivations in health, education, and standard of living.

points.en: Uses 10 indicators across 3 dimensions: Health (Nutrition, Child Mortality), Education (Years of Schooling, Attendance), and Living Standards (Cooking Fuel, Sanitation, Drinking Water, Electricity, Housing, Assets).
points.hi: Uses 10 indicators across 3 dimensions: Health (Nutrition, Child Mortality), Education (Years of Schooling, Attendance), and Living Standards (Cooking Fuel, Sanitation, Drinking Water, Electricity, Housing, Assets).

points.en: NITI Aayog publishes the National MPI for India.
points.hi: NITI Aayog publishes the National MPI for India.

points.en: It aligns with the global methodology but includes additional indicators relevant to the Indian context.
points.hi: It aligns with the global methodology but includes additional indicators relevant to the Indian context.

points.en: A person is multidimensionally poor if they are deprived in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
points.hi: A person is multidimensionally poor if they are deprived in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.

question.en: What is the threshold for being considered multidimensionally poor?
question.hi: What is the threshold for being considered multidimensionally poor?

answer.en: Deprivation in at least 33.3% (one-third) of the weighted indicators.
answer.hi: Deprivation in at least 33.3% (one-third) of the weighted indicators.

misconception.en: MPI is solely based on income levels.
misconception.hi: MPI is solely based on income levels.

correction.en: MPI is a non-monetary measure that captures overlapping deprivations in health, education, and living standards.
